name: Muscle setting (quad and glute sets)
pattern: Isometric squeeze: a muscle is tightened hard and held without the joint moving, often the first exercise after injury or surgery.
setup: Quad set: sit or lie with your leg straight, a small rolled towel under the knee if you like.
Glute set: lie on your back, or stand, legs relaxed.

steps.text: Tighten the thigh to press the back of your knee down (quad set) or squeeze your buttocks together (glute set).
Hold the squeeze about 5 seconds, breathing.
Let go fully, rest a couple of seconds, repeat.

cues.cue: Press the back of your knee down into the bed.
cues.why: This is the standard quad set; it switches the quads back on when swelling or pain inhibits them.

cues.cue: Watch the kneecap slide up as you tighten.
cues.why: A moving kneecap shows the quads are really contracting.

cues.cue: Squeeze your buttocks hard and hold 5 seconds.
cues.why: Regular 5-second glute squeezes improved hip extension strength as much as bridges in a training study.
Isometric holds can ease tendon pain; pain during the hold is a sign to ease off.

breathing: Breathe normally throughout the hold; never hold your breath.

tempo.note: Tighten in 1 second, hold 5, relax 2; about 10 reps, a few times a day.

mistakes.name: Lifting the leg
mistakes.looks: The heel or whole leg lifts off the bed instead of the knee pressing down.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heel on the bed; push the back of the knee down.
mistakes.why: Lifting uses the hip flexors and turns it into a leg raise.

mistakes.name: Knee stays bent
mistakes.looks: The kneecap does not move and the knee never flattens.
mistakes.fix: Try the other leg first to feel it, then use a towel under the knee to push into.
mistakes.why: The quads are inhibited; feeling the good side helps switch them on.

mistakes.name: Back arches
mistakes.looks: During a glute set the lower back lifts off the floor or arches in standing.
mistakes.fix: Keep your ribs down and squeeze only the buttocks.
mistakes.why: The back muscles take over from the glutes.

safety: After surgery follow your surgeon's or physio's plan; these are usually safe from day one.
Stop if the squeeze causes sharp pain.

variants.change: Standing glute squeeze: stand tall and squeeze, no movement.
Lying glute set on your back, legs straight or knees bent.
Towel under the knee: press down into it; inner-range version straightens the knee and lifts the heel.

easier: quad set with the leg supported

subtypes.name: Lying glute set
subtypes.change: On your back, legs straight; squeeze the buttocks together, the hips may rise a few millimetres.

subtypes.name: Standing glute squeeze
subtypes.change: Stand tall, squeeze the buttocks, knees soft; no movement.

motion.basis: Default is a right-leg quad set sitting propped on the elbows/backrest with legs straight (trunk -60, hips 60 estimated). Hold time and reps from fhft-knee; inhibition rationale from rice2010. Glute set from lehecka2019 (5-second maximal squeezes). Joint changes during a set are a few degrees and are exaggerated slightly for the animation.

sources.cite: Rice DA, McNair PJ. Quadriceps arthrogenic muscle inhibition: neural mechanisms and treatment perspectives. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2010;40(3):250-266.
